_source: Static UI keys for the mobile on-site material-issue screen (route field-stock, pototype/mobile-screens.jsx MFieldStock L484-528). NEVER a translation. ZERO-MINT: all five values already exist as dict ids in docs/extract/i18n-full.json today, so this slice touches the sacred file not at all and spends none of a Wei sacred round (the st_receive / field_gr precedent; BLOCKERS.md B-266 warns that minting copy which can never be backed wastes a round permanently). FIVE prototype strings have no honest key in any layer and are NOT rendered and NOT invented here - they are reported in BLOCKERS.md B-339 item 3 for a mint round (this sidecar previously cited B-328, an id that was NEVER ALLOCATED - grep -c "B-328" BLOCKERS.md returns 0 - so the mint round had never in fact been asked for). Two of the five back claims this screen DROPS outright (the QR/barcode scan trigger L493 and the return-material button L521 - neither has an endpoint, and minting copy for a control that can never work is exactly the waste B-266 warns about), so only three are worth a round: the header title, the basket section title and the CTA verb.
_layers: dict (t): title, itemsTitle, stockLabel, usedFor, confirm, queued, failed. No phrases-layer key is read by this screen - see _deviations on why the prototype's own warehouse name must NOT be one.
_lifecycle: queued and failed carry NO prototype copy at all - the prototype's buttons have no onClick, so it has no offline, no failure and no success state to port. They are the honest states a real at-least-once write can be in, and both keys are the ones merged st_receive already uses for the same two states, so the two screens cannot drift. queued = tax.etax.statusPending, th 'awaiting send', which is literally what a queued SyncOperation is. failed = admin.common.actionFailedToast, th 'action failed - try again'; the 'try again' half is honest HERE specifically because a permanent 4xx dead-letter is never replayed by drain(), so this screen's retry starts a FRESH op with a FRESH key (safe: a 4xx means the single-transaction handler wrote nothing). There is deliberately NO confirmed-state copy, and the reason is NOT st_receive's: this screen does NOT pop. It is a TAB BODY (mobile_shell.dart renders MobileScreenRouter as the tab body), so it is always Navigator.isFirst and maybePop would bubble past it and do nothing at all. The confirmation is the STATE CHANGE the screen can actually make - the staged quantities go back to 0, the CTA greys out, and the on_hand balances are re-read so the shelf no longer shows the pre-issue figures - all of which costs no key and asserts no unbacked success.
_deviations: THREE reuses that are not byte-exact, each checked against the sacred source this round, plus the rejections. (1) title = inv.issueAdd.title, th 'material issue OUT (Material Issue)' vs the prototype's bare 'material issue'. Semantically EXACT - it is the title of the web create form for THIS endpoint, the same act on the same document in the same module; the deviation is verbosity (a direction word the server's own -qty ledger row makes true, plus an English gloss), not meaning, so it cannot fabricate data or mislabel an action and it translates correctly in all four languages. (2) itemsTitle = inv.issueAdd.itemsTitle, th 'the items issued' vs 'issue list' - one syllable apart, the SAME slot (the item-list section title of the material-issue create form) for the same list. (3) confirm = common.confirm, th 'confirm' vs the prototype's 'confirm issue' - an UNDER-claim, the exact st_receive precedent. REJECTED, and the reasons matter more than the picks: (a) inv.issueAdd.btnSubmit, th 'save issue + cut stock', is the CTA of the web form for this very endpoint and was the strongest candidate - refused because this screen writes through the OFFLINE QUEUE, where a deferred outcome cuts NO stock; the label would be false on precisely the branch where the storekeeper most needs the truth. A button may under-claim what it does; it may never assert an outcome that did not happen. (b) inv.issue.subtitle contains the title inside a longer sentence. (c) gr.list.kpiReturns, th 'goods returned', for the return-material button: wrong noun (goods, not materials) AND a KPI-tile id a translator would fill as the noun 'Returns' - rejected for that second reason in B-324 too. (d) ap.retention.btnReturn, th 'refund', returns MONEY, not material. (e) composing inv.issueAdd.colIssue ('issue') with common.confirm ('confirm') to manufacture 'confirm issue' is INVENTING a translation - word order breaks in en/ar. A NEW TRAP, recorded because it is a class this codebase had not hit before: the prototype's eyebrow text 'warehouse Block B' (L487) IS present in the phrases layer with en/zh/ar already filled - but it is a SEEDED WAREHOUSE NAME (packages/db/src/seed/index.ts L754) that the extractor scraped out of the mock, not UI copy. Keying it would freeze one tenant's data into the interface AND translate a proper noun. It comes from warehouse_name on the wire instead. This differs from the near-miss rejections above: the string is a byte-exact hit in a real layer, and it is still wrong, because the failure is a DATA VALUE carrying a translation entry.
title: inv.issueAdd.title
